solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Arm Deva women?

definitions.meaning: a weapon, here a famous make of repeating rifle
Deva was the Roman name for Chester, so women (... describes the answer read as ...

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the women of a Roman town, as if asking whether they bore arms.
explanation.walkthrough: Deva is the Roman name for Chester, a city in north-west England. The second definition is cryptic: 'women (W) in Chester'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Winchester is a famous make of repeating rifle, and a rifle is a firearm, an arm; the city is also an English cathedral town.

clue.text: Sweep down bay tree, following wife's lead

indicators.note: following says the tree comes after the opening letter
lead means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: Instructions to clean under a bay tree, a wife taking charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bay' looks part of 'bay tree', but it is a second definition: The Wash, a bay on England's east coast. 'following' puts ASH after W.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that washes over something carries matter away, sweeping it downstream.

clue.text: One-nil, right? 5-1, then one-nil again: this will reduce excitement

parts.note: the word one with nil (O) taken away
Roman five, V, followed by Roman one, I
again, the word one minus nil, the letter O

explanation.surface: A tense football commentary on a scoreline swinging about, with a calming remedy offered.
explanation.walkthrough: The scores are arithmetic: 'One-nil' is ONE less O, and 5-1 is the Roman numerals V and I side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervine is a medicine that soothes the nerves, a sedative tonic to calm agitation.

clue.text: Drink strong liquor, zero downing soft drink — extremists of the group

indicators.note: downing means going down, so in this down entry the nought drops to a lower place

parts.note: hootch (or hooch) is slang for strong, often illicit, liquor
zero is the letter O
cola is a fizzy soft drink

indicators.note: extremists are those at the extremes, so the outer letters of the word

explanation.surface: A boozer downs strong spirits then a fizzy drink while the hardliners of the group look on.
explanation.walkthrough: HOOTCH is an alternative spelling; 'downing' moves one O lower, giving HOTCHO. The answer is also a pop group, which 'group' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm cocoa beverage is a familiar drink, often taken at bedtime.

clue.text: Clue: deal with outgoing correspondence

parts.note: to sign a document is to deal with it, putting one's name to it
post is the mail sent out

explanation.surface: An office instruction to handle letters waiting to be sent out.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer or indication giving guidance, as a roadside marker gives directions, is a clue.

clue.text: Might-have-beens ignore housing officer

indicators.note: housing means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Failed candidates are ignored when an officer is given accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' looks like accommodation but signals letters held inside 'Might-have-beens ignore'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior commissioned rank, historically the lowest infantry officer who carried the flag.

clue.text: Cut across square for fix

definitions.meaning: a hairstyle whose fringe is cut straight across the forehead
squarely or exactly, as in landing right on target
an injection of a drug, in slang

explanation.surface: Instructions for trimming something across a square to put it right.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: a straight-cut fringe (chiefly American), 'exactly' (as in 'bang on time'), and a drug addict's injection.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a dictionary meaning of the one word: fringe hairstyle, adverb for exactly, slang for a shot of drugs.

clue.text: Disbelieving, I am witnessing hold-up?

parts.note: to be at an event is to witness it
a heist is a robbery, a hold-up

explanation.surface: A bystander cannot believe they are watching a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a statement: someone who says 'I am disbelieving' of God.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who denies the existence of any god could say of themselves that they do not believe.

clue.text: Young lamb bit bird

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced
a shank is a cut of lamb from the leg

explanation.surface: A young lamb was nipped by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like the verb to bite, but 'lamb bit' is a piece of lamb, SHANK.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenshank is a wading bird of the sandpiper family with greenish legs.

clue.text: Dire straits get expert long-term planner

indicators.note: dire suggests something in a dreadful state, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A consultant is hired to rescue a business that has fallen on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dire straits' reads as a stock phrase, but 'Dire' is the anagram signal working on STRAITS and GET together.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist is someone skilled at planning overall campaigns over a long period, rather than short-term tactics.

clue.text: Go round hospital? I'm really enjoying it!

indicators.note: round says the word for go is placed around the hospital letter

parts.note: to go is a childish way of saying to urinate, to wee

explanation.surface: Someone on a fairground ride shrieks with delight as it circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' looks like the ride turning; in fact 'Go' means to wee, wrapped 'round' H.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what people shout for joy on a thrilling ride, so it stands for a cry of enjoyment.

clue.text: Quick chap to speak of order just after consuming krypton

indicators.note: consuming means the religious order eats up, so contains, the chemical symbol

parts.note: the Jacobins were French Dominican friars, a religious order
Kr is the chemical symbol for krypton
on means just after, as in following on

explanation.surface: A speedy fellow talks of a command given right after swallowing an element.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'before you can say' this name, meaning very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The name appears in the idiom for instantly, so this proverbial chap is the quickest man to speak of.

clue.text: In Wells, one hard up? Very much so

indicators.note: in tells us the numeral for one sits inside the writer's initials

parts.note: H.G. Wells, the novelist, gives his initials HG
the Roman numeral I stands for one
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A query about whether someone in the Somerset city of Wells is struggling, answered emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' looks like the cathedral city but is the author H.G. Wells. The definition is 'up' with the comment that it is very much so.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very much up, far above the ground, is lofty or elevated.

clue.text: Pain returning, she protects her pride in play

indicators.note: returning means the informal word for pain is read backwards

parts.note: gyp is an informal British word for pain, as in 'my knee is giving me gyp'
the mother (MA) of a lion pride protects her cubs: MA with LION

explanation.surface: A lioness, suffering, still guards her pride in some stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: GYP is informal British for pain; 'returning' turns it round. The protective mother of a pride is a MA LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's comedy about a phonetics professor transforming a flower girl is a well-known stage work.

clue.text: A rising poet on song is a supplier of convenience

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the poet's name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: T.S. Eliot, the poet
to troll is to sing in a carefree way

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming poet in fine form turns out to supply something handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on song' looks like 'in good form', but 'song' gives TROLL, to sing. 'convenience' is British for a public lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A public convenience is a lavatory, and a paper roll is what supplies it.

clue.text: Dig pecans to nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters before it go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to dig until they reach the pecans, or turn them into nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' sits naturally beside 'pecans' as if naming them, but it means crazy and signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Opencast mining is excavation from the surface rather than by shafts, so it describes a surface dig.

clue.text: Outline of square two-master

parts.note: a ketch is a sailing boat with two masts

explanation.surface: A drawing of a square-rigged sailing vessel with two masts.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough preliminary drawing or a brief summary gives the outline of something.

clue.text: Being ill at ease, it hurt in travel

indicators.note: in says the cry of pain goes inside the word for travel

parts.note: to fare is to travel, as in 'fare forth'
ouch is what one says when it hurts

explanation.surface: A traveller who is uncomfortable and in pain on the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Farouche means shy and sullen, awkward in company, so describes someone uncomfortable socially.

clue.text: Unwisely, in hindsight, Icarus was shot

definitions.text: Unwisely, in hindsight, Icarus was shot

parts.words: Unwisely, in hindsight, Icarus was shot
parts.note: Daedalus allowed his son Icarus to take wing, which proved foolish; the phrase also means fired, as a shot is

explanation.surface: A rueful verdict on the myth of Icarus, who flew too near the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: An implied double meaning: Icarus was permitted to take wing, unwisely as it turned out, and 'was shot' is the real definition, as an arrow is released.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a missile or a volley of words is to discharge it, which matches being shot.

clue.text: There's no worse place for retirement?

definitions.text: There's no worse place for retirement?

parts.words: There's no worse place for retirement?
parts.note: the colloquial phrase for the worst possible thing, with beds as a place to retire to at night, or racing cars retiring to the service area

explanation.surface: A grumble about a dreadful town to grow old in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests old age, but it is going to bed (slang 'pit') or a racing car pulling off the track into its service bay.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the very worst, so there could be nothing worse.

clue.text: A legendary flier clad in sheer, grainy dress material

indicators.note: clad in says the bird is dressed in, so sits inside, the word for sheer

parts.note: main as in 'by main force' means sheer, utter
the roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend

explanation.surface: A mythical bird is wrapped in sheer, grainy fabric, like a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheer' looks like a fabric word, but it means MAIN, as in 'main force'.
explanation.definitionFit: Marocain is a crinkled crêpe fabric with a ribbed, grainy texture used for dresses.

clue.text: Cuckold to be suitable for performance on time

parts.note: a play that acts well is suitable for staging, so act
an aeon is a vast stretch of time

explanation.surface: A betrayed husband is told he is fit to go on stage, and punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth this hunter was turned into a stag; his horns made him an emblem of the cuckold.
explanation.definitionFit: Horns were the traditional mark of a deceived husband, and this mythical figure grew antlers.

clue.text: Dry and sheltered place found by one PM

parts.note: one gives the indefinite article A
TT, teetotal, means dry
the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: A prime minister seeks a dry, sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee was Britain's Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.

clue.text: Shirt left on donkey's back — anything returned? A novel catch here?…

parts.note: a T-shirt gives T
left as in departed means went

indicators.note: back points to the final letter of the animal's name
returned means the dialect word for anything is read backwards

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: A shirt draped over a donkey, with a puzzled query whether anything came back.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is northern English dialect for anything; 'returned' turns it round to give the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Heller's novel is Catch-22, so the number pairs with a famous fictional catch.

clue.text: …a little bit, backing the first nine

indicators.note: backing means the letters are put in reverse order

parts.note: the first nine letters of the alphabet run A to I

explanation.surface: A continuation from the previous clue: only a small amount, supporting the first nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first nine' is the alphabet from A TO I; 'backing' turns that round. Fittingly this is also the ninth Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter is the smallest, so the word has come to mean a tiny amount or jot.

clue.text: Run odds Toughie setters raised

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds

indicators.note: raised in a down entry means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the setters of this puzzle speak of themselves as we

explanation.surface: Bookmakers offer odds after puzzle setters raise the stakes.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the starting price in horse racing, the odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: To spew is to pour or gush out, which is to run, as liquid does.

clue.text: Empty-handed angler's explanation providing late news?

parts.note: an angler going home empty-handed has caught nothing, the letter O
the fisherman explains what happened to the fish: one nibbled the bait, it bit

explanation.surface: A fisherman returning with no catch offers an excuse that reaches the newspapers late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late news' is crossword shorthand for a death notice; the angler's excuse is 'O (nothing) bit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice of someone's death is news about the late, the recently deceased.

clue.text: 'Disreputable one has no heroin', written across page?

indicators.note: written across says the words for has no and heroin are spread over the inside of the verb for page

parts.note: to beep someone is to page them on a pager
lacks means has no
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A quoted judgement on a shady character who is clean of drugs, scrawled across a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' looks like a sheet of paper but is the verb, to summon someone on a pager.
explanation.definitionFit: The family member who brings disgrace is a common idiom for a disreputable person.

clue.text: AI language, high-level — though is so influenced by having it!

definitions.meaning: a high-level programming language long used in artificial intelligence work

definitions.text: though is so influenced by having it!
definitions.meaning: a speech defect that turns S into TH, so 'is so' comes out as 'ith tho'

explanation.surface: A remark on computing jargon that comes out mangled in pronunciation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is illustrated by its own words: 'is so' said with this impediment.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the list-processing computer language and a speech impediment affecting sibilants.

clue.text: Nothing remote or futuristic about this (two-in-one?) present

definitions.text: Nothing remote or futuristic about this (two-in-one?) present

parts.words: Nothing remote or futuristic about this (two-in-one?) present
parts.note: the immediate place and time combined, a present that is neither distant in space nor in the future, two words for place and time joined

explanation.surface: A gift described as neither distant nor ahead of its time, perhaps a combination gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' sounds like a gift, but it means the present moment: not remote (so in this place) and not futuristic (so at this time).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the immediate present, this place and this moment, as opposed to some distant future.
